subject.title: Security: main agent can be removed via direct config edit, bypassing CLI protection

question: Should OpenClaw make literal `main` a required security invariant, or preserve arbitrary configured default-agent IDs and enforce generic referential integrity instead?
rationale: Current source treats `main` as the empty-config fallback and reserved CLI identity, while also intentionally allowing another configured agent to be the runtime default; choosing a stricter invariant changes a compatibility-sensitive configuration contract.

options.title: Validate generic references
options.body: Preserve custom default IDs, reject or diagnose missing effective defaults and dangling bindings, and repair only through doctor.

options.title: Require literal main
options.body: Make `main` mandatory, with explicit upgrade migration, doctor repair, documentation, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

options.title: Warn without blocking
options.body: Treat direct operator edits as trusted configuration and add doctor/startup warnings without rejecting or rewriting the configuration.

recommendation.title: Validate generic references
recommendation.body: Preserve custom default IDs, reject or diagnose missing effective defaults and dangling bindings, and repair only through doctor.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this person to both Gateway agent methods and the session-state surface affected by agent deletion and repair semantics.
